question: What makes the Vagus nerve (Cranial Nerve X) stand out from most other cranial nerves?

options.A: It controls the sense of smell entirely on its own.
options.B: It has no sensory function whatsoever.
options.C: It travels all the way down into the chest and tummy.
options.D: It only activates during high stress or panic.

explanation: Fantastic! While most cranial nerves stay around the head, the vagus nerve wanders down to supply our chest and belly organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T15#GNS211_U3_T15_h4)

question: What happens to bile between meals when your body doesn't need it right away?

options.A: It is filtered out by the kidneys and eliminated in urine
options.B: It is broken down into simple sugars by liver enzymes
options.C: It is stored and concentrated inside the gallbladder
options.D: It is sent back to the stomach to digest proteins

explanation: When you're not eating, your gallbladder acts like a storage pouch, holding onto bile and thickening it up until you eat something fatty and it's time to squeeze it out. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h4)

question: How does low staff motivation directly impact patient care on the ward?

options.A: It reduces the cost of medical equipment
options.B: It can lead to missed care and clinical errors
options.C: It forces administrators to hire more doctors
options.D: It automatically shortens the length of hospital stays

explanation: When nurses feel unmotivated or burnt out, it is easy to miss small details. Staying encouraged helps keep our patients safe! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h1)

question: How can biological sex directly affect how a patient responds to medication?

options.A: By changing the patient's personal gender identity overnight
options.B: By eliminating all potential drug side effects completely
options.C: By affecting how medications are metabolized and cleared in the body
options.D: By determining the exact cost of the prescription at the pharmacy

explanation: Spot on! Differences in organ size, body fat, and enzymes mean drugs can clear differently in male and female bodies. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h6)

question: How does disease surveillance differ from standard bedside nursing care?

options.A: Surveillance is only performed by doctors inside specialized laboratories
options.B: Surveillance deals exclusively with chronic genetic disorders
options.C: Surveillance requires advanced surgical skills instead of basic bedside observation
options.D: Surveillance focuses on population-level health trends rather than single patients

explanation: While bedside nursing cares for one patient at a time, surveillance looks at the big picture to protect entire communities. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h1)

question: In a busy clinic, how does a multi-dose medication vial usually get contaminated?

options.A: Using a previously used needle or syringe to enter the vial
options.B: Cleaning the rubber stopper with alcohol before every puncture
options.C: Storing the medicine bottle inside a warm medication refrigerator
options.D: Failing to shake the suspension liquid before drawing a dose

explanation: That's right! If a needle has touched a patient, using it to enter a shared multi-dose vial contaminates the whole bottle for everyone else. Always use a fresh, sterile needle and syringe! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is a big downside of relying only on an employer's group malpractice policy?

options.A: The nurse must pay a monthly maintenance fee directly to the hospital finance office
options.B: The policy limits are shared across the whole facility and can be exhausted by other claims
options.C: Group policies automatically convert to claims-made policies after six months
options.D: The insurance company dictates which hospital unit the nurse is allowed to work on

explanation: A group policy is like a shared pot of money for the whole hospital. If a huge lawsuit drains it, there might not be enough left to protect you. [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h5)

question: What does hormonal hypersecretion mean?

options.A: A complete stop in all hormone production
options.B: The excessive production and release of hormones
options.C: Normal hormone levels with sluggish target tissues
options.D: The destruction of endocrine glands by infection

explanation: Hypersecretion simply means an endocrine gland is making and releasing too much hormone into the blood. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h1)

question: In the epidemiological triangle, what does the 'host' refer to?

options.A: The human or animal that carries the infectious organism
options.B: The specific microorganism causing the sickness
options.C: The medication used to treat the infection
options.D: The physical climate where the outbreak takes place

explanation: Spot on! The host is simply the living creature—like you, me, or an animal—that provides a home for the disease-causing germ. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h2)

question: Why don't people usually have severe allergic reactions the very first time they meet a new trigger?

options.A: The body needs time to first build up and sensitize IgE antibodies to that trigger.
options.B: Allergens can only enter the bloodstream after the skin has been damaged twice.
options.C: The immune system is completely dormant until the third or fourth exposure occurs.
options.D: First exposures are always destroyed completely by normal white blood cells in the liver.

explanation: You got it! The first exposure acts as a rehearsal—it primes your immune system by creating those special IgE antibodies, which then react fiercely the *next* time you meet the trigger. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T8#GNS215_U6_T8_h1)

question: What must a researcher always get from a patient before collecting any study data?

options.A: Permission from local media
options.B: A monetary donation
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Medical insurance cards

explanation: Correct! Patients must always voluntarily agree to take part after fully understanding what the study is about. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h6)

question: What activities are normally included in a pulmonary rehabilitation program?

options.A: Supervised exercise training and breathing exercises
options.B: Continuous high-dose antibiotic therapy
options.C: Long-term isolation so the patient avoids all outside air
options.D: Surgical replacement of damaged lung tissue

explanation: Pulmonary rehab is wonderful for chronic lung patients! It combines guided physical activity and breathing techniques to help them breathe easier and build stamina. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h6)

question: During a suspected outbreak of an animal-borne disease, what is a key role for a nurse?

options.A: Manufacturing new chemical pesticides in a hospital laboratory
options.B: Reporting suspected cases and educating the community on prevention
options.C: Enforcing quarantine laws through police and military patrols
options.D: Designing blueprints for modern municipal drainage systems

explanation: You got it! Nurses are right on the front lines, helping catch outbreaks early and teaching people how to stay safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h7)

question: What defines experimental research in healthcare?

options.A: Researchers only watch patients without changing anything
options.B: Data is collected exclusively through old history books
options.C: Researchers actively give a treatment and use random groups
options.D: Studies are always performed on animals in cages

explanation: Spot on! In experimental research, researchers actively step in—giving a treatment and using random groups to test if a new method really works. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's bedside locker to clear out old, forgotten food brought by family?

options.A: Perishable foods lose all their carbohydrate value within two hours
options.B: Hospital policy forbids patients from eating food brought by relatives
options.C: Unrefrigerated perishable food breeds bacteria that cause food poisoning
options.D: Non-perishable items attract insects if left near hospital beds

explanation: You got it! Sick patients have weaker immune systems, so warm food sitting in a locker can quickly grow dangerous bacteria and cause tummy trouble. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h6)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance at the primary health care level?

options.A: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.B: To collect taxes from patients seeking medical treatment
options.C: To detect unusual increases in cases early and report them
options.D: To construct new hospital buildings in rural districts

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on health patterns so health workers can spot a sudden spike before it becomes a major outbreak. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h6)

question: What happens to the amount of virus (viral load) during the long, quiet chronic latency stage of HIV?

options.A: It drops to lower levels compared to the acute stage
options.B: It increases rapidly every single day
options.C: It remains exactly identical to the acute stage peak
options.D: It disappears completely from the bloodstream

explanation: Great job! During latency, the viral load settles down compared to the massive spike during early infection, though the virus is still quietly active. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h2)

question: What type of pen ink is recommended for writing in manual health records to ensure longevity?

options.A: Washable water-based ink
options.B: Pencil for easy erasing
options.C: Red ink for all entries
options.D: Permanent black or blue ink

explanation: Permanent ink ensures that records do not fade, smudge with humidity, or get easily altered over time. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand how drugs act at the cellular level?

options.A: To manufacture new pharmaceutical compounds in the ward
options.B: To bypass the need for regular patient vital sign checks
options.C: To anticipate both healing effects and unwanted side effects
options.D: To eliminate the requirement for physician prescriptions

explanation: Knowing how drugs work helps you stay one step ahead! It allows you to predict how the medicine will help your patient, and also watch out for any unexpected side effects. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of using standard anatomical terminology in nursing practice?

options.A: To ensure clear and accurate communication among healthcare workers
options.B: To replace the need for physical assessments in the ward
options.C: To make patient medical records harder for families to read
options.D: To provide complex billing codes for hospital management

explanation: Standardized terms prevent misunderstandings so that every nurse or doctor knows the exact location being discussed. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h1)

question: A patient asks why she noticed cervical changes after starting a new oral contraceptive pill. What is the best way to explain it?

options.A: The pill permanently scars the muscular walls of the uterus.
options.B: The pill causes the outer cervical skin to become very dry and crack open.
options.C: The hormone estrogen in the pill causes inner cervical cells to shift outward.
options.D: The pill creates a bacterial infection that eats away at the outer cervix.

explanation: Birth control pills contain estrogen, which signals the inner cervical cells to expand outward. Explaining this simply to your patients helps ease their worries completely! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: What was the main focus of early psychoanalytic therapy?

options.A: Isolating patients from stressful family environments
options.B: Training patients to change bad habits through rewards
options.C: Exploring hidden conflicts in the unconscious mind
options.D: Using electrical shocks to reset brain chemistry

explanation: Psychoanalysis aimed to bring repressed memories and hidden emotional struggles from the unconscious into conscious awareness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the common underlying problem in chronic brain diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's?

options.A: Acute bacterial infection inside the ventricular system
options.B: Complete destruction of the skull bone structure
options.C: Abnormal folding and accumulation of specific proteins
options.D: Sudden rupture of major cerebral aneurysms

explanation: In these conditions, certain proteins misfold and clump together into sticky clusters that slowly harm brain cells over time. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T19#GNS222_U3_T19_h6)

question: Which of these is a basic shared need that brings a community together?

options.A: Employment in corporate technology firms
options.B: Membership in international political parties
options.C: Access to clean water and basic healthcare
options.D: Ownership of luxury motor vehicles

explanation: Things like clean water, food, and basic health services are everyday priorities that unite everyone. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h5)

question: In clinical teaching, what does "scaffolding" mean?

options.A: A physical platform used to reach high equipment in simulation labs
options.B: The strict grading rubric used to penalize medication errors
options.C: Temporary support given to a student that is removed as skills improve
options.D: Memorizing drug dosages word-for-word before clinical placement

explanation: Just like builders use temporary scaffolding while putting up a house, your clinical instructors support you closely at first, then gently step back as you gain confidence! [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h4)

question: What do luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) directly do to the gonads?

options.A: Stopping the secretion of growth hormone during sleep
options.B: Shutting down the pituitary gland through negative feedback
options.C: Stimulating the production of sex steroids like estrogen and testosterone
options.D: Directly causing the closure of the epiphyseal plates in long bones

explanation: Great job! LH and FSH act like messengers to the ovaries and testes, telling them to start producing sex hormones. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is buying healthcare different from buying regular items like shoes or phones?

options.A: The price of medical care never changes based on economic factors
options.B: Patients can easily treat themselves without professional assistance
options.C: Healthcare items are always distributed by governments for free
options.D: People demand healthcare because they want health, not because it is a source of pleasure

explanation: Nobody wakes up wishing to visit the hospital for fun! We seek care simply to get our health back and function well. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which position is best when placing the rectal tip for a barium enema?

options.A: Sims' position (lying on the left side with right knee bent)
options.B: Supine position (flat on the back)
options.C: Prone position (lying flat on the tummy)
options.D: Lithotomy position (stirrups up)

explanation: The Sims' position naturally relaxes the anal sphincter, making the insertion smoother, safer, and much more comfortable for the patient. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why is water so crucial for chemical processes inside the body?

options.A: It is converted directly into stored body fat for warmth
options.B: It acts as a fluid medium for chemical reactions and transport
options.C: It slows down digestion so food stays in the stomach longer
options.D: It provides the primary source of daily dietary calories

explanation: Water is the ultimate carrier fluid. It provides the watery environment needed for chemical reactions and moves nutrients and waste all around the body. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T009#GNS227_U1_T009_h4)

question: Where does fertilization usually happen inside the fallopian tube?

options.A: Infundibulum
options.B: Isthmus
options.C: Ampulla
options.D: Fimbriae

explanation: Brilliant! The ampulla is the wide middle part of the tube where the sperm and egg love to meet. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why are some STIs tricky because they don't show any physical signs or symptoms?

options.A: Infected people can spread the disease without knowing they have it
options.B: Laboratory tests cannot detect pathogens if symptoms are absent
options.C: The body builds permanent immunity during the latent phase
options.D: Asymptomatic infections always resolve spontaneously without treatment

explanation: Exactly! When someone has no symptoms, they feel healthy and can unknowingly pass the infection to their partners. Good thinking! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which part of the ovary holds the developing egg follicles?

options.A: Medulla
options.B: Cortex
options.C: Fimbria
options.D: Fundus

explanation: The outer layer, or cortex, contains ovarian follicles in different stages of growth and maturation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: What term describes the final coming together of the male and female genetic material (chromosomes)?

options.A: Ovulation
options.B: Capacitation
options.C: Syngamy
options.D: Atresia

explanation: Syngamy is the exact moment the chromosomes from mum and dad finally mix together to form the unique genetic blueprint of the new baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h6)

question: Why do we carry an antiseptic solution like chlorhexidine in the infection prevention pack?

options.A: To act as an energy drink for tired mothers in labor
options.B: To serve as a nice jelly for easing dryness
options.C: To clean and prep the skin before exams or procedures
options.D: To quickly wipe down and clean rusty metal scissors

explanation: Antiseptic solutions lower the number of germs on the skin, which protects the mother and baby from nasty infections during delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why is teaching community members about injection safety so important in Nigeria?

options.A: To cut down the cost of running clinics
options.B: To replace nursing school training
options.C: To help patients understand they don't always need an injection
options.D: To teach patients to give themselves IV drugs at home

explanation: Many people believe injections work faster than tablets, leading to a huge demand for unnecessary shots. Educating the public keeps everyone safer. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which finding in a jaundiced newborn must be reported immediately because it points to bile duct disease?

options.A: Frequent crying during diaper changes
options.B: Clay-colored or pale stools
options.C: Yellow skin extending to the toes
options.D: Mild sleepiness between scheduled feeds

explanation: Stools that look pale or clay-colored mean bile isn't reaching the gut, which can signal a serious condition like biliary atresia. You are learning to spot the critical details! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h5)

question: A 38-week pregnant woman comes in complaining of tummy tightening that stops when she walks around. What is this likely to be?

options.A: signs of premature placental abruption
options.B: hypertonic uterine dysfunction
options.C: Braxton Hicks contractions
options.D: active phase labour contractions

explanation: Spot on! When contractions are irregular and go away with rest or walking, we call them Braxton Hicks or false labor. Nothing to worry about! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h1)

question: Which Nigerian law provides key legal protections against child abuse and exploitation?

options.A: The Federal Highway Traffic Code
options.B: The National Tax Administration Act
options.C: The Petroleum Industry Act
options.D: The Child Rights Act

explanation: Great job! The Child Rights Act is the foundational law that protects minors across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T3#GNS225_U5_T3_h8)

question: In many Nigerian clinical settings, what is a major hurdle that stops patients from getting their prescribed drugs?

options.A: An oversupply of specialized surgical instruments
options.B: Out-of-pocket spending by patients
options.C: Excessive availability of free hospital parking
options.D: Mandatory international travel for simple prescriptions

explanation: When patients have to pay cash directly for every drug without health insurance, buying medications becomes a serious daily struggle. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is a common non-infectious cause of cervical inflammation?

options.A: Increased dietary intake of refined sugars
options.B: Chemical spermicides and barrier devices
options.C: Normal fluctuations in monthly estrogen levels
options.D: Inadequate daily fluid consumption

explanation: Not all inflammation comes from germs! Things like chemical spermicides or barrier devices can irritate the delicate cervical tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h2)

question: How do major health authorities view the medicalisation of FGM?

options.A: As a helpful stepping stone toward total eradication
options.B: As an acceptable compromise for cultural preservation
options.C: As a severe violation of human rights and medical ethics
options.D: As a minor disciplinary issue handled by local clinics

explanation: Global organizations universally condemn medicalised FGM, viewing it as an unethical practice by trained professionals. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why must nurses know that a normal pregnant woman can have a high white blood cell count?

options.A: To determine the correct dose of routine iron supplements
options.B: To avoid misinterpreting a normal pregnancy change as a severe infection
options.C: To calculate the exact date when spontaneous labour will begin
options.D: To prove that the mother's immune system is completely shut down

explanation: Good nursing judgment! Knowing what is normal for pregnancy prevents us from panicking or treating a healthy mum for an infection she doesn't have. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h3)

question: As a nurse, what is the very first thing you do after a patient's test comes back positive?

options.A: Discharge the patient to home isolation
options.B: Interview the index patient to find contacts
options.C: Vaccinating the entire neighborhood immediately
options.D: Closing down public markets in the local area

explanation: Spot on! We start by talking to the main patient (the index case) to gently find out who they've been hanging out with recently. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h2)

question: Which cranial nerve gives movement (motor control) to almost all the muscles of the tongue?

options.A: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
options.B: Trigeminal nerve (CN V)
options.C: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
options.D: Facial nerve (CN VII)

explanation: Think 'Hypo-glossal' for tongue movement! It's the big boss nerve controlling almost all tongue muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is a key nursing priority when caring for a patient newly diagnosed with a uterine issue causing recurrent miscarriages?

options.A: Explaining that lifestyle choices are the sole cause of her congenital condition
options.B: Discouraging her from asking questions about future pregnancy attempts
options.C: Providing empathetic emotional support alongside clear education about treatment options
options.D: Insisting that the patient undergo immediate major surgery to remove the uterus

explanation: Spot on, nurse! This diagnosis can be heartbreaking. Patients need a compassionate ear just as much as they need clear, easy-to-understand medical facts. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h7)

question: What happens during a prescribing cascade?

options.A: The pharmacy runs out of basic supplies and substitutes vitamins
options.B: A drug side effect is mistaken for a new illness and treated with another drug
options.C: All medications are washed out of the patient's system at once
options.D: A nurse stops all prescriptions due to a sudden power outage

explanation: The prescribing cascade creates a dangerous cycle where side effects lead to more prescriptions instead of drug discontinuation. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a workplace risk assessment?

options.A: To evaluate how likely a hazard is to cause harm and determine appropriate controls
options.B: To replace all human workers with automated robotic machinery
options.C: To calculate the exact financial profit generated by each department
options.D: To find reasons to terminate employees who report minor injuries

explanation: Think of a risk assessment as looking ahead: we spot the danger, see how likely it is to hurt someone, and put rules in place to stop accidents before they happen. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h4)

question: What happens when surviving nephrons have to overwork because their neighbors broke down?

options.A: They regenerate completely to cure the disease
options.B: They stop working immediately to rest the kidney
options.C: They turn into normal liver cells
options.D: They undergo hyperfiltration and suffer further damage

explanation: Think of it like carrying extra load—when healthy nephrons take over for damaged ones, the heavy workload puts them under stress, wearing them out faster too. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T5#GNS213_U4_T5_h2)

question: Children playing barefoot in dirt can catch hookworm. What is actually happening in the soil?

options.A: The shed ova are maturing into infectious forms in the earth.
options.B: The soil is actively generating new adult worms without eggs.
options.C: The eggs are dissolving completely into harmless minerals.
options.D: The dirt is killing all parasites with natural plant toxins.

explanation: Warm, moist soil gives many parasite eggs the incubator time they need to become infectious to humans. Exactly right! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h4)

question: What special chemical is added to the blood collection tube for a fasting blood sugar test to keep the blood cells from eating up the sugar?

options.A: Potassium EDTA
options.B: Sodium fluoride
options.C: Heparin sulfate
options.D: Calcium chloride

explanation: Great job! Sodium fluoride acts as a preservative (glycolytic inhibitor) that stops red blood cells from consuming the glucose in the tube before the lab technician can test it. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which animal is the main natural home (reservoir) for the Lassa fever virus?

options.A: Common house cat
options.B: Domestic pig
options.C: Multimammate rat
options.D: Anopheles mosquito

explanation: You'll see this often in public health: the multimammate rat carries the Lassa virus and sheds it in its droppings, contaminating food around homes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h4)

question: As a general nurse working at Tier 3, which of these is your best intervention?

options.A: Performing electroconvulsive therapy
options.B: Prescribing complex antipsychotic drug cocktails
options.C: Performing neurosurgery for trauma
options.D: Delivering basic psychological first aid and supportive counseling

explanation: Spot on! Nurses at Tier 3 provide wonderful, comforting care like active listening and psychological first aid without needing a psychiatry degree. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is a major goal of physical therapy in the long-term management of a child with spastic cerebral palsy?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any assistive devices by age five
options.B: Preventing joint contractures and improving functional mobility
options.C: Permanently stopping all involuntary muscle contractions
options.D: Curing the underlying brain lesion through intense exercise

explanation: Physical therapy uses stretching, strengthening, and positioning to keep muscles pliable and prevent permanent joint tightening. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why do hospitals use standard clinical protocols?

options.A: To increase the paperwork load for night shift nurses
options.B: To eliminate all forms of natural patient diversity
options.C: To ensure every patient recovers in the exact same timeframe
options.D: To reduce unwanted differences in patient care

explanation: You've got this! Standardized protocols simply help guide our practice so that every patient gets safe, consistent care no matter who is on duty. Keep it up! [learn more](GST319_U2_T4#GST319_U2_T4_h1)

question: How can social and economic factors increase a woman's risk of getting an infection?

options.A: They frequently limit her ability to negotiate safe sex practices
options.B: They directly alter the chemical balance of cervical mucus
options.C: They prevent the body from producing natural antibodies
options.D: They speed up the reproductive cycle of common pathogens

explanation: In real life, lack of financial independence or social power can make it really difficult for a woman to insist on using protection like condoms. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h1)

question: A patient works in a chemical factory and is worried about fertility. Which background detail helps you catch this risk?

options.A: Religious affiliation
options.B: Home address
options.C: Occupation
options.D: Marital status

explanation: Spot on! Knowing what a patient does for a living helps you check if they are exposed to workplace toxins or heavy physical stress that could affect their reproductive health. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which management approach is most effective for retaining experienced clinical nurses?

options.A: Discouraging further education to keep staff on the ward
options.B: Providing a supportive work environment and clear career growth
options.C: Ignoring staff complaints to maintain strict discipline
options.D: Forcing nurses to work overtime without extra compensation

explanation: Nurses stay where they feel valued, supported, and given real opportunities to advance their careers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h7)

question: How would you best describe erectile dysfunction?

options.A: Inability to achieve or maintain an erection
options.B: Complete absence of male hormones
options.C: Involuntary loss of bladder control
options.D: Painful spasms during urination

explanation: Easy and clear! Erectile dysfunction simply means having trouble getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sex. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h3)

question: A student spends 12 hours a day playing online games, skips meals, and is failing exams. What does this point to?

options.A: Internet Gaming Disorder
options.B: Acute social anxiety
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Normal adolescent recreation

explanation: When gaming takes over someone's entire life and basic needs or responsibilities get ignored, it goes way beyond normal fun and fits Internet Gaming Disorder. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h2)

question: What main change happens inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) during pneumonia?

options.A: The walls permanently stretch and lose stretchiness.

question: Your nursing team tries a new handover checklist, but the run chart shows no improvement after two weeks. What should you do next?

question: Which of these is a key part of healthy sleep hygiene?

question: What is the main goal of reproductive coercion in a relationship?

question: Which of these is a classic example of a positive feedback loop?

question: Why can taking NSAIDs frequently lead to stomach ulcers?

question: Why is it so important to find the root cause of a gap found during an audit?

question: Which of these is NOT something you would typically see in a patient with chronic malabsorption?

question: As a nurse, what is your top priority when assessing someone with suspected food poisoning?

question: What is the primary purpose of formative assessment during a course?

question: What is the main difference between a hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

question: Which laboratory stain is used to spot tuberculosis bacteria under the microscope?

question: Why do different birth control methods have different follow-up timetables?

question: If a baby's head enters the pelvis leading with the longest chin-to-forehead (mentoventricular) measurement, what is the likely outcome?

question: How does knowing a client's psychiatric diagnosis directly help you as a nurse?

question: How do T-cell receptors interact with epitopes differently than B-cell receptors?

question: Why is checking the net fluid balance important after a rectal washout?

question: What is a common myth about secondary infertility that nurses should help correct?

question: What is assisted partner notification in HIV care?

question: Who founded the Henry Street Settlement and coined the term public health nurse?

question: Why are anthropometric measurements so helpful in busy or rural primary healthcare clinics?

question: What environmental factor triggers the skin to start producing vitamin D?

question: Why do doctors treat active tuberculosis with several drugs at once instead of just one?

question: In a published research paper, where can you usually find recommendations for future studies?

question: Why is it important to involve traditional and religious leaders when promoting girl child education?

question: Which side effect often happens when drugs like metoclopramide and promethazine block dopamine in the brain?

question: Which sign strongly suggests a patient is struggling to swallow during a meal?

question: If a patient takes a drug that blocks muscarinic receptors, what bodily response would you expect?

question: A nurse checks clinic attendance registers to see which illnesses bring patients in most often. What is this called?

question: Why do you usually need two healthcare workers to measure the length of a baby?

question: What is the most crucial assessment for a nurse to do regularly on a limb with a tumor or post-op reconstruction?

question: When a patient is injured by a medical error, why do they often sue the hospital along with the nurse?

question: Which complication is a major cause of death for stroke patients who have trouble swallowing?

question: Why is addiction considered a chronic brain disease instead of just a lack of willpower?

question: During the dry season in northern Nigeria, a patient presents with a very stiff neck, high fever, and confusion. What should you suspect first?

question: What is the main job of a second-order neuron in a sensory pathway?

question: Why do some polycythaemia patients feel very itchy after a warm bath?

question: Why do nurse researchers collect data in a study?
